_about: Public-domain George Hickes (1642-1715), Dean of Worcester, deprived in 1690 and consecrated a nonjuring bishop, for the Word Hoard: the Two Treatises on the Christian Priesthood and the Episcopal Order (Library of Anglo-Catholic Theology, 1847, three volumes) and his controversial works in early printings, from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 40 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

hickes-two-treatises-1: Two treatises on the Christian priesthood and on the dignity of the episcopal order : with a prefatory discourse in answer to a book entitled The rights of the Christian Church, &c., and an appendix, vol. 1 (Oxford : J.H. Parker, 1847)
hickes-two-treatises-2: Two treatises on the Christian priesthood and on the dignity of the episcopal order : with a prefatory discourse in answer to a book entitled The rights of the Christian Church, &c., and an appendix, vol. 2 (Oxford : J.H. Parker, 1847)
hickes-two-treatises-3: Two treatises on the Christian priesthood and on the dignity of the episcopal order : with a prefatory discourse in answer to a book entitled The rights of the Christian Church, &c., and an appendix, vol. 3 (Oxford : J.H. Parker, 1847)
hickes-jovian-1683: Jovian. Or, an answer to Julian the apostate.  1683 (catalogued 1683)
hickes-spirit-of-enthusiasm-1709: The spirit of Enthusiasm exorcised: In a sermon with two discourses ... the first "the history of Montanisme" by Dr. Lee ... the other "the new pretenders" ... by N. Spinckes (catalogued 1709)
hickes-controversial-discourses-1727: A collection of controversial discourses by G. Hickes and a popish priest (catalogued 1727)

_alternates.hickes-copies: Other scans of the 1847 Two Treatises (Toronto, Google) and the 1707 and 1711 printings; other copies of each early work

_excluded.hickes-other: The Thesaurus of the northern languages (1703-1705, Latin philology); Devotions in the Ancient Way of Offices (1846), John Austin's book as Hickes reformed it; Fenelon's Instructions for the Education of a Daughter and the Gentleman Instructed, which he translated or prefaced
